header.status_line: Transmission is THIN: 1 reconstructed record for Mark 16 -- 8 degrees from the origin event, composed ~70 CE at 'Rome', mode 'narrative'. It is an honest FRONTIER aspect (a definition + one worked, reconstructed record, not a scaled run) and it earns no green scale pill. Renamed from 'Witness' (Decision 224).

what_it_is: Transmission answers ONE question: how far is the text you are reading from the event it reports, and through what chain did the report travel? A 'witness' (an eyewitness, or a manuscript that attests the text) is ONE rung of that chain; Transmission names the whole chain -- the degrees of separation from the origin event, the year + place of composition, the FORM the report travels in (narrative / creed / conceptual-node / apocryphal), and the material ecology of the surviving witness (scribe, literacy, power-context, format, marginalia).
why_it_matters: Two texts can make the same claim at very different distances from the event -- an eyewitness report and a fourth-hand creed are not the same evidence. Transmission is what keeps that distance visible, so a late, heavily-transmitted text is not read as if it were an eyewitness. It also guards the other aspects: a feature that is a transmission artifact (a scribal change, a translation shift) is not misattributed to the author.

how_it_works.you_give_it: a text + what is known of its composition + transmission history.
how_it_works.the_method_does: reconstructs the transmission graph (source / redaction criticism), estimates the degrees from the origin event + the composition year/place, classifies the mode, and records the material ecology of the witness -- flagging the whole thing as a reconstructed ESTIMATE, never a measured value.
how_it_works.you_get_back: a text-level transmission record + a degrees-from-origin number that feeds the Degrees-of-separation output.

pipeline_context.note: sibling terms glossed so the card stands alone.
pipeline_context.Situate: the parent node: attaches context to each move; Transmission is its 'distance-from-the-event' aspect.
pipeline_context.degrees of separation: how many transmission hops separate the text from the origin event (this text: 8).
pipeline_context.how the number is counted: it is NOT a coder's judgement call: the coder names the transmission CHAIN (the engine writes each link to transmission_edge), and compute_witness_degrees_s161.py then DERIVES the number as the shortest path in hops from the graph's 'ORIGIN' node to this text. So one hop = one edge the coder asserted in the chain. Code the chain; do not type the number (the engine's prompt tells the coder to leave degrees_from_origin null for exactly this reason).
pipeline_context.why the number is provisional: the engine flags this scalar PROVISIONAL because it conflates three unlike things into one integer: an uncountable oral stage, a contested pre-composition written source, and the copying chain. The review panel wants it RETIRED in favour of a typed chain, which is a schema restructure still owed. Read it as a rough ordinal, never a measurement, and prefer 'unknown' to false precision.
pipeline_context.the origin event: the event or utterance the text reports (here, the resurrection appearances it narrates).
pipeline_context.mode: the FORM the report travels in: narrative / creed / conceptual-node / apocryphal.
pipeline_context.material ecology: the physical conditions of the surviving witness: scribe, literacy, power-context, format (scroll->codex), marginalia.
pipeline_context.a witness (textual criticism): a manuscript that ATTESTS a text; one rung in the transmission chain (the eyewitness is the earliest rung).
pipeline_context.stemma: the family-tree of a text's manuscripts/sources, reconstructed to infer how far the surviving text is from the original.
pipeline_context.reconstructed estimate: the honest status of this record -- derived from a stemma / source-criticism (Markan priority, Q, the early creed), NOT a measured value.
pipeline_context.PI: the principal investigator (the researcher) -- who locked the Witness -> Transmission rename (Decision 224).

the_method_clean.note: Transmission's fields: mode is a closed enum; degrees + year are numeric; place is open; material ecology is a structured JSON; the whole record is flagged a reconstructed estimate.

fields.note: the form the report travels in: narrative (a told story) / creed (a fixed confessional formula) / conceptual-node (a compressed idea/title passed as a unit, e.g. 'Son of Man') / apocryphal (an extra-canonical transmission)
NUMERIC -- hops from the origin event (an estimate)
how the position was derived (stemma-reconstructed) + honesty flag (reconstructed-estimate)
JSON: scribe / literacy / power_context / format / marginalia

material_ecology.note: Greek manuscript tradition on papyrus and parchment codices; earliest substantial witnesses are 4th-c. majuscules (Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, both of which END Mark at 16:8) plus 5th-c. Alexandrinus and later Byzantine mss carrying the Longer Ending (16:9-20); the passage 16:9-20 is text-critically contested (absent, obelized, or accompanied by scribal notes in a significant witness stream, and by the Shorter Ending or both endings in others); transmitted within a Christian scribal culture of professional and semi-professional copyists, lectionary use, and eventual codex-Gospel collections; translated early into Latin, Syriac, Coptic; quoted patristically (Irenaeus knows a form of 16:19) — so the transmission stream is plural and text-critically layered, not a single line

the_method_applied.note: Mark 16's transmission record (render-from-data): 8 degrees from the origin event, composed ~70 CE (Rome), narrative mode, stemma-reconstructed. Every value is a reconstructed ESTIMATE (basis = 'reconstructed-estimate'), not a measurement.

run_and_record._this_is_the_agent_spec: everything needed to RUN this engine and record a result, in one block. The rest of the card is written for a human reader; nothing there is required to act.

black_box_contract.reads: see the engine script's header contract.
black_box_contract.writes: see the engine script's header contract.
black_box_contract.upstream: Decompose (source_move) must already have run for this key; Situate refines an existing moveset.
black_box_contract.gates: the run tag names one run, never a text; CHECK-constrained values are coerced against the vocab SSOT before write; an empty model response fails loud rather than writing a partial batch.

run_and_record.how_to_read_the_pills: a pill is the verdict of one DATED run, not a live status; where it and the card body disagree, the body is current. whats_next is generated fresh on every build.

before_you_run.decompose_first: Situate codes a text Decompose has already broken into moves, and the move-grain aspects read that moveset directly. Against an empty moveset a run does not error, it silently produces nothing. Check: SELECT COUNT(*), MAX(run_tag) FROM source_move WHERE source_key='<key>';
before_you_run.the_text_file: --text-file takes plain UTF-8. The reproducible way to make one is the LIBRARY checkout (shared_terms.text_checkout); a hand-pasted file works once but flag it in evidence_basis.
before_you_run.the_card_builder_is_mark_16_only: the CODERS run on any text; the drawer BUILDERS have the Mark 16 keys hardcoded and take no arguments. A new text can be coded and queried today, but its card cannot be generated, so its Cold Read cannot run. The parameterised builder is owed.

naming_conventions.run_tag: <textslug>_s<session>_<YYYYMMDD>, e.g. mark16_s170_20260813. One tag per RUN, not per text, so a re-code never overwrites an older run. Lands in: transmission_record.run_tag (a real column on this store). Older rows carry pre-convention tags (form_v1_s168, witness_s161, ood_s168) — historical, do not copy, and the reason a query must name its run.
naming_conventions.deployed_drawer_file: ../grammarofmeaning-site/engine/data/goldenpath/<text_slug>/transmission_node_drawer.json — the SIBLING deploy repo (what other cards call DEPLOY_REPO), not this one. text_slug is the source_key lowercased without punctuation: MARK-16-WEB -> mark16, MARK-16-GRC -> mark16_grc, TTC-CH1-EN -> ttc_ch1. A new text needs its directory made first (mkdir -p).
naming_conventions.cold_read_run_doc: pm/30_methodology/engine/COLDREAD_situate_transmission_run_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md — run_cold_read.py writes it and prints the path. Pass --date or the filename carries the wrong day.
naming_conventions.vs_wild_run_doc: pm/30_methodology/engine/VALIDATION_situate_transmission_vs_wild_run_<YYYY-MM-DD>.md — YOU write this one. The runner only drops the wild arm in field_ed/_persona_engine/out/situate_vs_wild/; the comparison against the instrument arm is yours to write, and seed_card_check.py fails loud if the cited file is absent.
naming_conventions.the_account_flag: --account hds picks which Claude Max plan the SDK call uses (Tier 1, $0). Check it is live first: ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/lib/sdk_account_refresh.py hds --check

how_to_record_a_verdict.step_1: run the Cold Read: ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/analysis/run_cold_read.py --node situate.transmission --drawer-file <the deployed drawer json for this text> --date <YYYY-MM-DD> --account hds  (it prints the COLDREAD run-doc path it wrote; see naming_conventions).
how_to_record_a_verdict.step_2: add ONE ROWS entry to scripts/analysis/seed_card_check.py of exactly this shape:

rows_entry_shape.run_doc: <the COLDREAD run-doc path run_cold_read.py just printed>

how_to_record_a_verdict.step_3: run ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/analysis/seed_card_check.py  (it FAILS LOUD unless the cited run_doc exists on disk); the verdict lands in card_check and renders as the pill. Seeding just means adding that ROWS entry and running the script: there is no other step.
how_to_record_a_verdict.the_bar: PASS = a fresh reader can RUN the engine from this card (Cold Read) and FIND where the prior work lives (Cold Start), with no broken gaps, honest limits flagged, and the card TIGHT — a reader should not be able to cut a third of it without loss. Not zero-clarifications: close the broken gaps, flag the limits, cut the padding, stop.

how_to_run_vs_wild.what_it_asks: does our scaffolding beat the same text read by an unscaffolded LLM given none of the instrument's fields. Primary metric is RELIABILITY (do repeated runs agree), not eloquence. Scope the wild arm to ONLY this aspect's job: an unscoped wild reader borrows the other layers' work and appears to win.
how_to_run_vs_wild.step_2_instrument_arm: this aspect's coded rows, already in its store. Comparison protocol: pm/30_methodology/engine/VALIDATION_situate_vs_wild_RUNSHEET_s170_2026-08-11.md.
how_to_run_vs_wild.step_3_record: record it like a Cold Read, with check_name 'vs_wild'.
how_to_run_vs_wild.for_a_new_text: PROMPTS in the runner is {aspect: prompt}; copy an entry and swap the text's name. It currently holds sitz / transmission / lineage, all written for Mark 16.
how_to_run_vs_wild.honest_limit: per §2.14 the DECISIVE run is on an UNDERSTUDIED text. On Mark 16 a naive model scores well from memory of the commentary, so parity there measures recall, not the instrument.

foundation_codes._what: the honesty tags on EVERY Situate coding, whatever wrote it. C4/R7 = evidence_basis + certainty (on what basis, how sure). C8/R3 = scope_level (at what grain). Grammar situate_foundation_v1, rendered from scripts/lib/situate_foundation_vocab.py.

evidence_basis (C4/R7).external-material: archaeology / epigraphy / material culture attests it.
evidence_basis (C4/R7).scholarly-consensus-with-citation: the field agrees AND a real citation is attached (corpus/DR only, never LLM memory).
evidence_basis (C4/R7).strongly-inferred: the coder reasoned it from strong, multi-source warrant (not from the coded text alone).
evidence_basis (C4/R7).internally-inferred: inferred FROM the text being coded — the context-laundering flag; downstream may EXCLUDE.
evidence_basis (C4/R7).LLM-proposed: a model proposed it with no external warrant (make the LLM-ness visible, §2.8).
evidence_basis (C4/R7).contested: the field actively disagrees; there is no settled basis.

certainty (C4/R7).low: the coder would not defend this value against a competing reading; treat as provisional.
certainty (C4/R7).med: the coder's best reading, but a competing reading is live (record it in alternative_hypothesis).
certainty (C4/R7).high: the coder would defend this value; no live competing reading at this grain.

scope_level (C8/R3).text: the whole source — the coding is a property of the work, not of any one part of it.
scope_level (C8/R3).pericope: the source's NATIVE sub-division (Mark 16:1-8 vs 16:9-20). Where no native division is marked, fall back to the Connect bundle / spine-segment — do NOT invent a new pericope primitive (R3).
scope_level (C8/R3).move: a single move (one operation plus its arguments), as produced by Decompose.

foundation_codes.alternative_hypothesis (C4/R7): OPEN free text: the competing reading the coder rejected. Expected whenever certainty is low or med.

shared_terms.text_checkout: the LIBRARY's package of a text, and the mandated read path: verbatim (byte-identical to the stored passage text, hashed), anchored (carries {source_id, passage_id, verse_markers}), and versioned (a pinned snapshot). Engines code the checkout OFFLINE rather than reading the live DB, and results ingest back joined on the anchor. Build one with: ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/analysis/build_checkout_package_s162.py --source-id <id> --ref "Mark 16" --out <path>  (optional: --verse-prefix / --section-prefix to pick the in-text markers, --edition WEB, --version v1). It resolves a source already in-corpus and chunked.
shared_terms.move: one operation plus its arguments: the derived sense-unit Decompose produces. Distinct from a passage, which is the source's own container (verse, pericope, paragraph).
shared_terms.wild: an unscaffolded LLM read of the same text, given none of the instrument's fields. The control arm.

methodology_tags.§2.1: code from the text's own terms; do not force a pre-set label (anti-pre-anchoring).
methodology_tags.§2.8: bias-visibility: name the conditions so corpus skew stays auditable, not hidden.
methodology_tags.§2.14: test the method out-of-domain (an understudied text), not only the one it was tuned on.
methodology_tags.§2.16: render from data: the card is generated from the coding, so it cannot silently drift.
methodology_tags.§2.13: single store of record: canonical data lives in a DB table (mirrored to Neon), not a loose file.
